newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes mixed ahead of pipe scheduling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes mixed ahead of pipe scheduling.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were mixed late Friday as refiners scrambled to cover last-minute March needs ahead of the pipeline scheduling deadline early next week, traders said.
The March/April WTI spread was last heard done around 20 cents a barrel, putting March WTI/Cushing around $21.60 a barrel, down 30-40 cents from late Thursday's cash market.
The spread traded earlier at a high of 44 cents and a low of 17 cents a barrel, traders said.
The grades fluctuated in a continued divergence of sweets and sours.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked around WTI/Cushing plus 35-40 cents a barrel, a few cents strongoer than late Thursday. An April deal was heard at 22 cents premium.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire continued to pick up steam among the few large players involved. The grade was talked at plus 45-50 cents a barrel, with 38 cents last heard done.
WTI/Midland was at minus 45-40 cents a barrel, down three to five cents from late Thursday.

Sour crudes continued to plummet on weak fundamentals. West Texas Sour/Midland was last bid at $2.85 under WTI/Cushing, down 45 cents from late Thursday's bids. An April deal was transacted at minus $2.30.
Eugene Island was around $2.35-2.20 a barrel, down five to 10 cents from late Thursday. The grade was last done at $2.20.
Posting Plus eased with the spread to $2.00-2.05 a barrel, down from $2.28 earlier in the day.
